mappings.note: Five true/false claims split across three outcomes: (i)+(ii) are the work definition (LO-1), (iii) is the joule as unit of energy (LO-4), (iv)+(v) are forms of energy and interconversion (LO-5). No single outcome covers the item.

Blanks (i)+(ii) recall the work definition and the joule (LO-1), (iii)+(iv) recall the KE and PE expressions (LO-5), and (v) recalls power as a rate, which sits in C-2.6-LO-1's define-power clause. All three are recall, none is calculation, so no LO-2/LO-6.

The gradeable energy claims are 'KE is zero' and 'PE is maximum' at the top of a vertical throw - the free-flight PE/KE interchange of LO-7. The force and acceleration distractors are prior-chapter mechanics with no outcome here.
Asks the defining requirement for work (displacement along the force). Straight recall of the definition, so LO-1; nothing is computed, so not LO-2.

Pushing an immovable wall: zero displacement means zero work, decided purely from the definition (LO-1). Part of the zero-work family that honestly shares this outcome; muscular fatigue is a distractor, not an energy-forms question.
Perpendicular force does zero work - the direction clause of the work definition (LO-1). Not LO-2: the answer is a direction judgement, not an evaluation of F x s.

Goalkeeper's force opposes the ball's displacement, so the work is negative - again the definition's direction clause (LO-1). Deliberately NOT the work-energy theorem (LO-3): the item never mentions the ball's kinetic energy change.
The discriminating statement is that the SI unit of work is the newton (false) - the 'and its SI unit' clause of LO-1, which is why this sits with LO-1 rather than the energy-unit outcome LO-4.

Assertion-reason on the perpendicular-force case; the reason is the definition of work itself, so LO-1. Same outcome as the girl-carrying-box MCQ - the pair genuinely shares one outcome, only the format differs.

The entire question is a mechanical-advantage comparison (MA = length/height) between two ramps; the ramps are already identified, so LO-3 is not tested. C2.6 is the ONLY legal code naming mechanical advantage - the frame has no LO for it.

Work as the area under a force-displacement plot: LO-2 for obtaining work from the expression, LO-71 for reading it off a graph. Not LO-3, which is only invoked when the work is converted to a kinetic-energy change.
A four-way match of scenarios to energy transformations - the interconversion clause of LO-5. Matching lists are not data to interpret, so no LO-71 here unlike the tabular items.
Recites the work-energy theorem itself (net work equals change in energy) - LO-3 verbatim, and the only item in this batch that states rather than applies it.
Fills two cells of a PE/KE/total table for a freely falling sphere: LO-7 for the free-fall interchange keeping the total fixed, LO-71 because the reasoning is done by reading across a data table.
Recall of the expression 1/2 mv^2 - the 'define kinetic energy and derive its expression' clause of LO-5. LO-6 would require substituting numbers, which this item never does.

Area under a VARIABLE force graph equals the kinetic energy gained - that identification is the work-energy theorem (LO-3), plus LO-71 for the graph. Distinguished from the constant-force graph item, which stops at work (LO-2).
Quantitative proportional reasoning with 1/2 mv^2 (double v, quadruple KE) - using the expression to get a number, so LO-6 rather than the definitional LO-5.

Solved by the lever moment balance (load x load arm = effort x effort arm), i.e. mechanical advantage, which only C2.6 names; LO-3 for the seesaw as a lever. Not an energy outcome - no work or energy value appears.
Statements 1, 3 and 4 test what KE is and what it depends on (LO-5); statement 2 tests that its SI unit is the joule, i.e. the unit-of-energy clause of LO-4. Recall throughout, so no LO-6.

Four rows of force/displacement/relative-direction data must be read and the negative-work row inferred: the sign rule is LO-1, the row-by-row table inference is LO-71. No arithmetic is required, so not LO-2.

Picks out which forces in a free-body diagram do zero work - the perpendicular clause of the work definition (LO-1). A labelled force diagram is not data to interpret, so unlike the table items this earns no LO-71.

The reason offered is the squared velocity in the KE expression, so the item is testing the expression itself (LO-5). LO-4 would fit only if the general concept or unit of energy were the point; here it is specifically the KE formula.
Computes mgh/t for four machines from a data table and compares: calculating power is C-2.6-LO-2, and the four-row comparison is LO-71. Not C-2.6-LO-1, which covers only defining power.

Names the form of energy stored in a deformed bow (elastic potential) - the 'name forms of energy' clause of LO-5. Deliberately not the gravitational-PE clause: no height is involved, which is exactly the distractor.

Ranks four ramps by MA = length/height from a data table. Mechanical advantage has no LO in this frame, so C2.6 carries it; LO-71 for the tabular comparison. Same outcome as the two-ramp MCQ - this family honestly shares it.
